findings.summary: revoke uses list.remove, which scans the list, so each logout is O(n) in the number of live sessions.

judge.reason: Matches known problem: O(n) list.remove in revoke.

findings.label: valid_other

findings.summary: purge_expired deletes list items one at a time, shifting the tail each time, so a purge can cost O(n·k); rebuilding the list in one pass would be O(n).

judge.reason: Deleting items one at a time costing O(n·k) is a real but minor performance concern, though not a correctness bug; it is a legitimate efficiency observation and doesn't contradict the key's correctness note.

findings.label: valid_other

findings.summary: The store has no locking, so if purge_job runs in a scheduler thread, concurrent revoke and purge_expired calls could race, e.g. a KeyError on del self._by_token[session.token].

judge.reason: Matches known problem: store has no locking and could race under threads.
